headline: Anduril confirms its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
summary: Defense contractor Anduril and Qualcomm are partnering to build laptops entirely in the US, starting in 2027. Anduril now commits to 65% US-made components for its BlueChip laptop at launch.
details: Defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm have announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States. Their first model, the BlueChip laptop, is slated for release in 2027. This initiative aims to establish a fully domestic supply chain for the computer industry over time.

Anduril's VP of communications, Shannon Prior, confirmed that the BlueChip laptop will feature at least 65 percent US-made components by its 2027 launch. This commitment aligns with the updated Buy American Act, which requires products to have a minimum of 65% domestic component cost to be considered US-made. The threshold will increase to 75% in 2029.

Initially, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey had stated the percentage of US-made components was "TBD" when questioned by The Verge. This new commitment clarifies a significant detail regarding the laptop's compliance. Luckey had previously expressed a long-term goal of 100% domestic manufacturing.

Meeting these standards is crucial for selling to federal agencies, many of which are legally required to purchase American-made computers. Currently, many government procurements happen under waivers due to a lack of compliant options. Anduril aims to address this gap with its BlueChip laptop.
